question.problem:
Consider the function $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}.$  The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}g(x)}{(x+8)^{7}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{4}+2x})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+8)^{6}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{4}+2x-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+8)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}+2x-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+8)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =4{x}^{3}+2-6\cdot \frac{1}{x+8} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}(4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}(\frac{(4{x}^{3}+2)(x+8)-6}{x+8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{7}}((4{x}^{3}+2)(x+8)-6) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{7}}(4{x}^{4}+32{x}^{3}+2x+16-6) \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}(2{x}^{4}+16{x}^{3}+x+5)}{(x+8)^{7}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)=2{x}^{4}+16{x}^{3}+x+5.
$$
